newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Jan 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Jan 13.

text.p: The Japan Securities Dealers Association (JSDA) plans to allow margin trading of some over-the-counter (OTC) issues as early as the summer to boost investment by individual investors and to help companies to raise funds.
The JSDA is expected initially to allow margin trading of a little over 100 of the 762 OTC shares.
Mitsui & Co Ltd and NEC Corp have won a 16 billion yen order to install 380,000 phone lines in Uzbekistan. The project will be partly financed by Japanese government lending.
The project is part of the Uzbekistan government's plan to triple phone lines to 4.2 million lines by 2010 at a cost of more than 200 billion yen.

Toyo Engineering Corp has received an order to design a refinery for a Thai oil distributor. The company will also most likely handle construction of the refinery, making the total value of the order at more than 100 billion yen. The refinery, to be built in the Songkhla region of southern Thailand, will have production capacity of 125,000 barrels of crude oil a day.

General Motors Corp is rapidly expanding its market share in Japan and was the leading importer in 1996. The GM group's sales in Japan rose 20 percent year-on-year in 1996 to 71,500 vehicles, mainly due to robust sales of models produced by its German unit Opel.
